headline: Fragment-ion evidence limits de novo peptide sequencing and PTM localization
label: De Novo Peptide Sequencing Benchmarks
summary: Eight deep learning de novo models share errors from limited fragment coverage, as new tools shift toward constraining search and localization.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that peptide identification from MS/MS is bounded by fragment-ion evidence. A benchmark of eight deep learning de novo peptide sequencing models on three proteomics datasets reports shared errors tied to limited fragment coverage, indicating that model architecture alone does not resolve sequence ambiguity. Other items address related bottlenecks from different angles: Carafe applies deep learning fragment-ion intensity prediction to prune the Comet fragment ion index, reducing index memory and speeding tandem MS database searches; MS Andrea scores PTM combinations per PSM in open searches using sequence tags; onsite provides an alanine-decoy FLR framework for phosphosite localization; and CasanovoGUI offers a cross-platform desktop interface to Casanovo. What is new is the shift toward constraining the search and localization space, though none of these items establishes fragment-ion evidence as an explicitly validated quantity.
